Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace
(
née
Byron
; 10 December 1815 – 27 November 1852), also known as
Ada Lovelace
, was an English
mathematician
and
writer
chiefly known for work on
Charles Babbage
's proposed mechanical general-purpose
computer
, the
analytical engine
. She was the first to recognise the machine had applications beyond pure calculation. Lovelace is often considered the first
computer programmer
.
Lovelace was the only
legitimate child
of poet
Lord Byron
and reformer
Anne Isabella Milbanke
.
